shouldFix.title: v8 records ADV-V7-01 as REPAIRED, but the substituted sentence is falsified by v8's own enumerated closed roster, and the repair the advisory actually named was not performed
shouldFix.finding: v7 read 'They are on the v4 roster so a later status-only refresh cannot leave the parsed half behind', where 'They' is the enumerated set decision, owner, sourcePin, acceptanceEvidence, consequence, status. v8 rewrites this to 'They sit on this generation's closed roster so a later status-only refresh cannot leave the parsed half behind.' That is false in these bytes. This generation's closed roster is enumerated verbatim at /basedOn/method and contains exactly two registerRowCarriedWhole paths: /registerRowCarriedWhole/source and /registerRowCarriedWhole/parsedCellsDerivedFrom. It does not contain /registerRowCarriedWhole/decision, /owner, /sourcePin, /acceptanceEvidence, /consequence, or /status. The same roster sentence adds 'Every path neither the roster nor succession metadata names is unchanged from v7', and my leaf diff confirms all six of those cells are indeed unchanged — i.e. the document both asserts the six cells sit on the roster and demonstrates that they do not. There is no alternative referent for 'closed roster': the phrase occurs only at /basedOn/method and at /reviewGuidance/forTheIndependentReviewer/17, which points at the same enumeration. Separately, the substitution does not perform the repair ADV-V7-01 named. That advisory's whyNotShouldFix stated the repair explicitly: 'Repairing it means restating the guarantee as a standing rule rather than as roster membership.' v8 preserved the roster-membership framing and only repointed which generation's roster is invoked — which, given that the advisory's core observation was that rosters here are closed per generation and therefore confer no forward protection, makes the guarantee weaker rather than stronger: a roster that expires with this generation cannot constrain the 'later status-only refresh' the sentence is about. Despite this, /honestyRepairsFromV7/1 reports the fold as done and /predecessorVerdictFindings/v7/claude2/findings/0/disposition records ADV-V7-01 as 'REPAIRED'.
shouldFix.failureScenario: A successor generation reads /honestyRepairsFromV7 and /predecessorVerdictFindings, sees ADV-V7-01 disposition REPAIRED, and does not revisit it. File 08 later moves; that successor rosters /registerRowCarriedWhole/status for a status-only refresh, relies on the parsedCellsDerivedFrom sentence as the guarantee that the derived half travels with it, and leaves decision, owner, sourcePin, acceptanceEvidence and consequence stale against the new rowVerbatim. The guarantee that was supposed to prevent exactly this never existed, and the ledger says it was repaired.
shouldFix.whyShouldFixAndNotAdvisory: The v7 reviewer withheld SHOULD-FIX on this issue against an explicit test — 'No defect exists in these bytes. The guarantee is merely weaker than its wording suggests' — and that was correct at v7, where the sentence made a historical claim about v4's roster and nothing had drifted. v8 fails that same test. The claim is now present-tense and self-referential, and it is refuted by an enumeration inside the same file, so the defect is in these bytes rather than latent in a future one. The honesty ledger is the second half of the defect and the more consequential half: this corpus's succession discipline depends on honestyRepairs* plus predecessorVerdictFindings being an accurate account of what a generation did, and an entry marking REPAIRED for a repair not performed is an honesty defect in an artifact whose declared discipline is honesty accounting. That is a different class from the legibility observation ADV-V7-02 was.
shouldFix.whyNotBlocker: Nothing downstream is exposed. The artifact binds NOTHING at DO-NOT-SEAL, status CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, and DR-105 stays OPEN. No measurement is wrong: file 08 has not moved (1cdcf9d4… reproduces), rowVerbatim is byte-exact against live line 287, and all six parsed cells are consistent with that row as measured, so nothing has actually drifted. No ENFORCED cell moved and no forbidden act was performed. The candidate is not invalidated; it needs a wording and ledger repair on a successor.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: On a successor, take either branch and correct the ledger to match. (a) Restate the guarantee as a standing rule that does not depend on roster membership — e.g. that the six cells are derived views of rowVerbatim and any generation that refreshes rowVerbatim or status must re-parse all of them — which is what ADV-V7-01 named. Or (b) keep the roster framing and make it true by placing /registerRowCarriedWhole/decision, /owner, /sourcePin, /acceptanceEvidence, /consequence and /status on that successor's closed roster alongside parsedCellsDerivedFrom. Either way, /honestyRepairsFromV7-equivalent and predecessorVerdictFindings must describe what was actually done. Preserve the current pins, the byte-exact carried row, the unchanged truth tables, and all non-application and open-standing constraints.

So the claim CLAUDE-V8-S1 identifies has been asserted and never grounded across v3, v4, v7 and now v8. This is an advisory and not part of the SHOULD-FIX because v8 correctly declares honestyRepairsFromV2..V6 historical and does not rewrite them, and because the /honestyRepairsFromV3 entry is scoped to v3 and cannot be read as a claim about v8. The third does not. v8 rewrote parsedCellsDerivedFrom to claim the six parsed register-row cells 'sit on this generation's closed roster', but the roster enumerated at /basedOn/method contains only /registerRowCarriedWhole/source and /parsedCellsDerivedFrom, so the document refutes its own sentence; and ADV-V7-01 had explicitly named the repair as restating the guarantee as a standing rule rather than as roster membership, which was not done. That is an honesty-ledger defect in an artifact whose declared discipline is honesty accounting, which is why it clears the advisory bar the v7 reviewer applied — the claim is no longer historical and weak, it is present-tense and false in these bytes. It is not a blocker: nothing binds, DR-105 stays OPEN, and no measurement is wrong. One narrow wording-and-ledger repair on a successor clears it.
